claim: A current-mode step-down converter using Type-III compensation should target a crossover frequency around one-fifth of the switching frequency and a 60-degree phase margin at crossover.
stance_target: compensation-loop design practice for buck converters
scope_conditions: current-mode step-down (buck) DC/DC converter, TPS40055 controller example
quoted_support: it is a good practice to try to reach a crossover frequency of one-fifth of the switching frequency, fSW... a good practice is to target a phase margin of 60 degrees at the crossover frequency.

claim: The PMP5532revB reference design using the TPS40055 wide-input synchronous buck controller achieved measured efficiency of up to 95%.
stance_target: achievable efficiency for wide-input-voltage synchronous buck converters
scope_conditions: PMP5532revB board, TPS40055 controller, 8V-40V input range
quoted_support: the report provides the calculations needed to estimate the power losses including an example that achieves up to 95% efficiency.

claim: Type-III compensation requires only two extra components compared to Type-II compensation while improving crossover frequency and phase margin for current-mode converters.
stance_target: choice of compensation topology for buck converter control loops
quoted_support: Type-III compensation is simple to design and needs only two extra components compared to a classic Type-II compensation.
